headline: Samsung Galaxy Ring gets FDA approval for advanced sleep apnea detection
summary: The smart ring now uses AI to detect breathing disruptions per hour, offering new insights into sleep quality and potential sleep apnea.
details: Samsung's Galaxy Ring has received FDA approval for an advanced sleep apnea detection feature, announced recently. This upgrade allows the device to detect the frequency of breathing disruptions each hour of sleep, providing users with more detailed information about their sleep patterns.

The feature was approved by the FDA in July, building on the initial De Novo authorization received in February 2024. While the original approval covered moderate to severe sleep apnea symptoms, the new version leverages AI for more granular analysis.

To use the feature, users need to sleep for at least five hours over two nights within a ten-day period. The Samsung Health Monitor app then analyzes the data to indicate whether the user experiences mild, occasional, or frequent sleep apnea.

Samsung emphasizes that while the Galaxy Ring can provide valuable insights and lead to productive discussions with healthcare professionals, only a physician can provide a definitive sleep apnea diagnosis.

This advanced sleep apnea detection is also available on the Galaxy Watch 9 and will be rolled out to the Galaxy Watch 7 and Galaxy Watch 8 via software updates. This feature sets the Galaxy Ring apart from competitors like Oura and Superhuman, which currently do not offer FDA-approved sleep apnea detection.
